_comment: CI fails on any advisory NOT listed here, so adding an entry is a deliberate,
reviewable act — not a silent suppression. Each entry must say why the
advisory cannot bite THIS codebase, verified against actual usage rather than
the advisory text, and what would make it bite (the tripwire).
`reviewBy` does not fail the build; it prints a loud warning once passed, so
an acceptance cannot quietly become permanent. Established by the 2026-07-29
had accumulated unreviewed since the last pass and the gate had been red on
master for some time. Each was verified against real usage — imports checked,
not advisory text read — and none is exploitable here. The stale react-router
entry (GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2) was removed: the advisory no longer matches, so
keeping it would have made the list lie about what it is protecting.

allow.title: Quill XSS via HTML export feature
allow.why: Axoview DOES call the affected getSemanticHTML(), but every call site pipes the result through sanitizeHtml() before it is stored (TextBoxInlineEditor.tsx:115,134), the model is re-sanitized on load (useInitialDataManager.ts:85), and the sole dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink re-sanitizes at render (TextBox.tsx:254,336). ADR 0029's defence-in-depth absorbs the payload.
allow.noForwardFix: npm's only remedy is a BREAKING downgrade to react-quill-new@3.7.0.
allow.tripwire: If the ADR 0029 sanitize is removed from ANY of those three points, this becomes live stored-XSS. renderedGeometry-style contract coverage on sanitizeHtml call sites would make that unmissable.

allow.title: brace-expansion DoS via exponential-time expansion
allow.why: devDependency only, reached via nodemon. Never bundled, never served, never processes user input.
allow.tripwire: brace-expansion appearing under a runtime dependency.

allow.title: brace-expansion DoS via unbounded expansion length (OOM)
allow.why: devDependency only, reached via nodemon. Never bundled, never served, never processes user input.
allow.tripwire: brace-expansion appearing under a runtime dependency.

allow.title: brace-expansion: DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation
allow.why: Test/build tooling only. `npm ls` puts it under jest → @jest/reporters → glob (axoview-app) and under the backend's dev tree; no workspace lists it as a runtime dependency (worker deps are hono alone; backend deps are cors/dotenv/express/helmet). The patterns it expands are our own glob literals in configs, never user input.
allow.tripwire: brace-expansion appearing under a runtime dependency, or any code path expanding a user-supplied brace pattern.

allow.title: DOMPurify: IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable, causing XSS
allow.why: DOMPurify is a shipped lib dependency, but the advisory needs two things this codebase never does: sanitizing with the IN_PLACE option, and removing a hook mid-flight. `IN_PLACE` appears nowhere in the repo, and utils/sanitizeHtml.ts registers exactly one hook (`addHook('afterSanitizeAttributes')`) at module scope and never calls removeHook/removeAllHooks. The precondition cannot be assembled.
allow.tripwire: Any use of the IN_PLACE option, or any call to removeHook/removeAllHooks — most likely if sanitizeHtml ever grows a second, conditionally-registered hook.

allow.title: Hono: ReDoS in CORS middleware via Access-Control-Request-Headers
allow.why: Hono ships in the worker, but the CORS middleware does not. The worker imports exactly three things from hono — `Hono`, `hono/body-limit`, `hono/secure-headers` (src/app.ts:1-3) plus the `Context`/`Next` types in src/auth.ts. `hono/cors` is never imported, so the vulnerable middleware is not in the bundle.

allow.title: Hono: memo() retains SSR output across requests, leading to cross-user data disclosure
allow.why: The worker is a JSON API with no server-side rendering: it imports no hono/jsx surface and calls no memo(). Verified by the same import audit as the CORS entry — only Hono, body-limit and secure-headers are imported.
allow.tripwire: Introducing hono/jsx or any SSR rendering in the worker.

allow.title: Hono: Proxy Helper does not remove response headers listed in the Connection header
allow.why: The worker does run an anonymous Drive read-proxy (ADR 0042 §2), but it is hand-written over fetch with an explicit response-header allowlist — it does not use Hono's `proxy()` helper, which is never imported. The advisory is scoped to that helper.
allow.tripwire: Replacing the hand-rolled read-proxy with `import { proxy } from 'hono/proxy'`.

allow.title: Hono: Algorithmic Complexity DoS in Language Middleware
allow.why: The language middleware is not imported. The worker performs no content negotiation — i18n is entirely client-side in axoview-app. Same import audit as the other three Hono entries.

allow.title: JS-YAML: Quadratic CPU consumption in !!omap resolution (3.x and 4.x)
allow.why: Test tooling only: js-yaml@3.15.0 is reached through ts-jest → @jest/transform in axoview-app. It parses Jest's own configuration at test time, never user input, and is not present in any shipped bundle.
allow.tripwire: js-yaml appearing under a runtime dependency, or any product code parsing user-supplied YAML.

allow.title: undici vulnerable to downstream response desynchronization via retry interceptor
allow.why: undici@7.28.0 is dev tooling — it arrives via wrangler → miniflare, the LOCAL Worker emulator. Production Workers run on Cloudflare's own runtime fetch, not npm undici, and no workspace declares undici as a runtime dependency. It never handles production traffic.
allow.tripwire: undici becoming a runtime dependency of the worker or backend, or miniflare being used to serve anything but local development.

allow.title: undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure and parse-time crash via degenerate private cache directives
allow.why: Same reachability as GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524: wrangler/miniflare dev tooling only. There is no multi-user cache in a local emulator run, so the cross-user half of the advisory has no analogue here.
allow.tripwire: undici becoming a runtime dependency of the worker or backend.

allow.title: undici vulnerable to CRLF Injection via blob-like body 'type' property
allow.why: Same reachability as the other undici entries: wrangler/miniflare dev tooling only, never in a shipped bundle and never handling production requests.
allow.tripwire: undici becoming a runtime dependency of the worker or backend.

allow.title: undici vulnerable to cross-user information disclosure via whitespace around equals in Cache-Control directives
allow.why: Same reachability as the other undici entries: wrangler/miniflare dev tooling only.
allow.tripwire: undici becoming a runtime dependency of the worker or backend.

allow.title: undici vulnerable to cookie attribute injection via unsanitized domain and unparsed setCookie fields
allow.why: Same reachability as the other undici entries: wrangler/miniflare dev tooling only. Axoview sets no cookies through undici — the worker's auth is bearer-token based (ADR 0043).
allow.tripwire: undici becoming a runtime dependency of the worker or backend, or cookie-based auth being introduced.
